answer: Each agent may act, but reputation is earned only when a randomly selected counterparty later confirms a completed task, and confirmation is weighted by the counterparty’s own history of reliable, costly work. A newcomer’s claims therefore carry little weight; a swarm of fresh identities cannot validate itself. To gain influence, an attacker must recruit established participants or fund many real transactions and risk losing stake when challenged—far more costly than minting names. Like an ocean tide, trust shifts gradually, not with a splash of pigment.
